newsitem.title: INDONESIA: Jakarta call money eases to 15.5/16.0 percent.
newsitem.headline: Jakarta call money eases to 15.5/16.0 percent.

text.p: Jakarta call money edged down to 15.5/16.0 percent from 19.0 percent on Thursday morning.
Dealers said initial worries of possible tightening due to the month-end factor did not materialise, pushing overnight rates lower, supported by a central bank offer of repos on its papers.
Bank Indonesia offered repos on one-week central bank certificates (SBIs) at 13.75 percent for Thursday.
Dealers said a net balance of 696 billion rupiah available from the maturing papers helped cool the market.
One dealer said arbitrage opportunities for banks with sufficient net open positions were still possible due to interest rate differentials between the swap and money markets.
Overnight swap was at 0.2/0.3 and tom/next at -0.1/par.
Overnight dollars were slightly high on Thursday at 10.0 percent after stabilising on Wednesday to seven percent.
The central bank remained cautious with its money policy, sustaining relatively high interest rates for short-term rupiah in the wake of extended currency instability in the region.
The rupiah weakened on renewed pressure in the Thai baht ahead of the announcement of some economic indicators.

The bank offered overnight bilateral SBIs at 14.0 percent, four-to-six day at 12.0 percent, one-week at 10.0 percent, two-week at 10.5 percent, one-month at 11.125 percent, three at 11.0, six at 11.625 and one-year at 12.25 percent.
Bank Indonesia remained absent from the short-term securities (SBPUs) market.
Dealers said longer-term money was slightly high due to relatively expensive short-term rates. One- and three-month money were at 17.25/17.5 and 17.00/17.25 percent, respectively.
The average overnight interbank rate on Wednesday was 17.42 percent, compared with 17.47 percent on Tuesday.
